title: Attribute-driven analytics access gate for console usage views
creator: Jonas Schmidt
description: Introduce an attribute-driven access gate for analytics endpoints and usage views in the Redwood Console backend. Current role-based checks are coarse-grained and rely on duplicated middleware across endpoints. This initiative implements an attribute-based access control (ABAC) layer that evaluates request attributes (requestor role, team_id, project_id, cost_center, read_window, token_scope) and resource attributes (view_id, dataset_tier, sensitivity) to compute allow/deny decisions. Goals: centralize permission logic, enable temporary/time-limited grants, support delegation (team admins granting view access), and ensure auditability and least-privilege defaults. The gate must be performant (sub-ms in the hot path for high-frequency usage endpoints) and compatible with existing entitlement-syncer and analytics query proxy components.
acceptance_criteria: All analytics read endpoints route through a single ABAC middleware that returns allow/deny decisions based on request and resource attributes
Supported attributes include: user_id, user_role, team_id, project_id, token_scopes, view_id, dataset_tier, sensitivity, and request_time_window
Administrators can create time-bound grants scoped to team/project/view via API (and UI in a follow-up ticket)
ABAC decisions are logged to audit-events with decision metadata (attributes, policy_id, decision, reason) for downstream compliance and retention
Latency increase of analytics endpoints < 10% p50 and p95 stays within SLA (target: <5ms added median overhead), validated under representative load
Backwards compatibility: existing role-based overrides continue to work during rollout and are configurable via feature flag
Unit and integration tests cover positive and negative policies, delegation flows, and policy precedence rules
Deployment includes a migration plan to backfill view metadata and dataset sensitivity tags for existing analytics views
implementation_notes: Add a central analytics-abac service module responsible for policy evaluation using a lightweight policy engine (Open Policy Agent inspired DSL but embedded; avoid external OPA server for hot path)
Store view metadata (view_id -> {dataset_tier, sensitivity, owner_team, default_visibility}) in the analytics-config DB table; provide migrations to populate from console metadata store

Policy examples to implement: allow team_admin to read all team views; allow user with token_scope:analytics:read and matching team_id to read project-scoped views; allow time_bound_grant entries with expiry checks
Integrate with entitlement-syncer for up-to-date role/team mappings; cache evaluations keyed by (user_id, view_id, token_scope) with short TTL and explicit invalidation on grant changes
Audit events pushed to existing audit-log topic with schema: event_type, actor_id, target_view, attributes, policy_id, decision, reason, timestamp
Expose a diagnostics endpoint (internal only) to fetch last-evaluation metadata for a request_id to help debugging and incident triage
Feature flag "analytics_abac_enabled" to toggle ABAC gate per environment and allow staged rollouts
api_changes: GET /internal/analytics/grants?team_id= - list grants for migration and audit
Middleware: analytics-abac-evaluate(request) invoked in analytics query proxy and console usage routes
Audit event schema addition: analytics_abac_decision emitted to audit stream
migration_plan: Add analytics_config table migration (view_id, dataset_tier, sensitivity, owner_team, default_visibility)
Backfill script: read console view registry and set dataset_tier and sensitivity. Default to 'standard' tier and 'low' sensitivity when unknown
Run backfill in read-replica during off-peak; verify counts and sample rows before switching gate on
Create grant for existing admin roles so they keep access during rollout
Feature flag rollout: start in dev, then staging; enable on 10% of production traffic; monitor errors and latency; full enable when thresholds met
testing_notes: Unit tests for policy evaluation engine covering combinatorial attribute rules and precedence
Integration tests simulating analytics query proxy calling the ABAC middleware with cached and uncached evaluations
Load test scenario that mirrors typical console usage (dashboard loads, CSV exports) to verify added latency and cache hit rates
E2E test to validate audit events are emitted and contain required fields
Security fuzzing to ensure malformed attributes are handled safely (deny by default)
rollout_plan: Deploy analytics-abac module behind feature flag to staging and run smoke tests
Enable flag for 10% production traffic and monitor: error rate, p95 latency for /usage endpoints, cache hit ratio, audit-event throughput
Iterate on caching TTLs and cache keys to reduce hot-path latency
On stable metrics, expand rollout to 50% then 100% and remove legacy role overrides after 2 weeks
Coordinate with Console UX team for follow-up ticket to expose grant management UI
